correctness.rationale: For an off-level point \(p=((i,a),(j,b))\), the proposed survivor at level \(\min\{i,j\}\) is below \(p\). Under lexicographic deletion, any strict predecessor outside the anti-diagonal has already been deleted, while every remaining anti-diagonal predecessor lies below that proposed witness; hence each deletion is genuinely down-beat. The survivors consist of two incomparable orientations at every level and all lower levels precede all higher levels, so the survivor poset is exactly the original minimal sphere. It has no beat points, proving it is the core. I independently replayed the deletion criterion for \(2\le n\le8\), obtaining point/deletion/core counts \((30,24,6)\) through \((306,288,18)\), while the universal quantifier rests on the order argument rather than the finite check.

value.rationale: Minimal finite spheres are canonical test objects for finite homotopy, and configuration spaces are a natural operation that need not preserve finite-space homotopy in a formal way. final_claim: For every \(n\ge2\), the ordered two-point configuration space of the \(2n+2\)-point minimal finite sphere strongly deformation retracts onto an anti-diagonal copy of the same minimal sphere, obtained by deleting all \(4n(n+1)\) off-level points as down beat points; this survivor is the Stong core.
limitations: Ordered configurations of exactly two points in the canonical minimal finite sphere model only.
